next_question: Change the object being measured from a STATIC fraction to a DYNAMICAL one, because this packet showed the static framing is not answerable on the substrate actually available. Stop asking what FRACTION of action-gating objects is re-derivable from one unconditional root GET, which is a per-site markup property whose measurement keeps dying on an uncalibrated site screen, and ask instead, for every candidate item of interface state a persistent agent would have to carry, WHICH STATIONARITY CLASS it belongs to and what it costs to RE-ACQUIRE a fresh valid instance. Concretely, with no new infrastructure (stdlib HTTP only, GET only, no browser, no docker, no model key, no write verb, no credentials): over K >= 5 independent fresh sessions with disjoint cookie jars per frozen target, classify each detected state item into a preregistered stationarity class, session_invariant, session_scoped, request_scoped, time_scoped, rotating, by exact-value and body-hash repetition, and measure re_acquisition_cost in cl100k_base tokens and request count for one unconditional path to a fresh valid instance; report the class distribution with a site-clustered interval and a resulting break-even reuse count per class, with token-to-latency and token-to-dollar remaining explicitly UNKNOWN. FALSIFIER, preregistered and arithmetically checkable before freeze: if the majority of detected state items are non-stationary AND re-acquiring a fresh instance is not cheaper than unconditional re-derivation of the path, then a handle-refreshing persistent state buys no measurable work reduction on the credential-free public HTTP substrate class, and the honest architecture answer is that persistent cross-episode state has no amortization surface THERE. That is a bounded negative for HANDLE PERSISTENCE in this substrate class only, and it closes neither C-CROSSSITE nor C-FRESHNESS nor the persistence question nor the Web. Both outcomes are decision-changing: mostly-stationary items make the refresh term bounded and computable, which is the precondition C-CROSSSITE economics has never had, while mostly-non-stationary items force SPIDER's persistent state to be restricted to session-invariant selector knowledge with a mandatory re-acquisition step, which is a concrete architecture change rather than a re-measurement.
